clue.text: Hit back with a whip

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the word for hit round so that it reads from right to left

parts.note: to swat is to hit sharply, as at a fly

explanation.surface: Someone retaliates by lashing out with a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SWAT round. TAWS is a Scottish word for a leather strap once used to punish schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: Taws is a leather strap with split ends, a kind of lash used for punishment.

clue.text: Weapon enables beastly male to catch a big bird

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a male cat
a hawk is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A weapon lets a male animal seize a large bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used as a weapon by Native North Americans.

clue.text: Agenda for education in German school

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the word for the German school

parts.note: Schule is the German word for school

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a programme for teaching at a school in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or list of things to be done, much like a plan of business.

clue.text: Humble lieutenant takes a letter

parts.note: a sub, short for subaltern, is a junior army officer such as a lieutenant
a missive is a letter or written message

explanation.surface: A modest junior officer receives some post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is only a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being humble means being meek and deferential, ready to yield to others.

clue.text: Fight with detectives for a load of junk

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or scuffle
the Yard, short for Scotland Yard, is the home of London's Metropolitan Police detectives

explanation.surface: A brawl with police officers over a heap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, so 'the Yard' stands for its detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapyard is a place where discarded metal and other rubbish is heaped up.

clue.text: Restarting the crossword

parts.note: a crossword grid is made of numbered squares, so going back to the very first numbered cell is a literal way of saying starting again from scratch

explanation.surface: A solver gives up and begins the puzzle all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to the starting point after an effort fails, and a grid's first numbered cell is that starting point.

clue.text: One who hits out-at a blackleg?

definitions.text: One who hits out-at a blackleg?

parts.words: One who hits out-at a blackleg?
parts.note: read as one who hits, it is someone who strikes a ball or a blow; read with the blackleg, it is a worker on strike who attacks the strike-breaker

explanation.surface: A picket turns on a worker crossing the line.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is British slang for a worker who keeps working during a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker is both one who delivers blows and a worker refusing to work, the natural enemy of a strike-breaker.

clue.text: Living luxuriously in the Cape with one's paramour

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Cape on maps
a paramour is a lover, often an illicit one

explanation.surface: Someone lives the high life in South Africa with a mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in comfort and prosperity, like cattle in a rich pasture.

clue.text: The obvious place to eat in Germany

definitions.text: The obvious place to eat in Germany

parts.words: The obvious place to eat in Germany
parts.note: the German verb meaning to eat is spelt the same as a city in the Ruhr, so that city is jokingly the natural spot for a meal

explanation.surface: A traveller asks where best to dine in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a large German city whose name is also the German infinitive for having a meal.

clue.text: She nurtures young lepidopterist!

definitions.meaning: a female parent who rears her offspring
jokingly, someone who studies or hunts moths

explanation.definitionFit: A parent caring for children is the usual sense; the whimsical second sense makes it a moth enthusiast.

clue.text: Fancies learning what an accountant costs

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
prices are the costs of things

explanation.surface: Someone is curious to discover an accountant's fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learning what' is link wording between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Caprices are whims or sudden fancies.

clue.text: Delay caused by armed robbery

definitions.meaning: a hitch or ... in traffic or progress
a robbery at gunpoint, as of a bank or stagecoach

explanation.surface: A wait caused by a bank raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is both a stoppage that slows things and a raid by gunmen.

clue.text: Recorded having filched a duvet

definitions.meaning: wrote down notes, as in a dictation
stole a quilt filled with feathers, taking the down

explanation.surface: Someone noted they'd stolen a quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something down is to note it in writing; jokingly, it is also to steal feathers or a quilt.

clue.text: Guide offers a great deal to Jack

parts.note: loads means a great deal, lots
a jack tar, or just tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A guide gives plenty of help to a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A loadstar (lodestar) is the pole star used by navigators, hence any guiding principle.

clue.text: George gets to car-parking lot after one

indicators.note: after places the word lot following the letter for one

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man called George goes to the car park after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: George is RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot; 'gets to' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang named the automatic flight control system George.

clue.text: Monarch served with beer and cabbage

parts.note: K stands for king, as in chess
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A king's dinner of beer and cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a variety of cabbage with curly leaves.

clue.text: Tear Alec to pieces

indicators.note: breaking things to pieces means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rip a man named Alec apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pieces' rearranges TEAR plus ALEC, and the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear flesh, so ripping Alec apart does exactly that.

clue.text: Superior spanner

definitions.meaning: something that spans a gap, such as a curved structure over an opening

explanation.definitionFit: Arch is a prefix meaning chief, and it is also a curved structure bridging a space.

clue.text: Reprove Scotsman embraced by a stunning looker

indicators.note: embraced by tells us the Scotsman piece sits inside the other words

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
mon is a Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A Scot is told off while held by a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to reprimand or scold gently.

clue.text: Things broadcast about American electioneering

indicators.note: about here means one piece goes around the other
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of things are rearranged

explanation.surface: Items are aired about an American election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges THINGS into HTINGS, and 'about' puts it around US.
explanation.definitionFit: The hustings are the platform and process of campaigning for votes before an election.

clue.text: Fair point admitted by a theologian and modified

indicators.note: admitted by means the fair point piece is let inside the other letters

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
just means fair
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A divine concedes a reasonable argument and changes his view.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted means altered slightly to fit.

clue.text: A stripper in excellent physical shape

parts.note: ace means excellent
muscle tone is physical condition

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer is very fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is a solvent that strips nail varnish or paint, not a dancer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a solvent used to remove paint and nail varnish.

clue.text: White veneer can be made any time

parts.note: WH is an abbreviation for white

indicators.note: can be made suggests the letters of veneer are made into something new

explanation.surface: A white veneer can be produced at any time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges VENEER into ENEVER, placed after WH.
explanation.definitionFit: Whenever means at whatever time.

clue.text: Wife takes large ring with cry of glee

parts.note: a hoop is a large circular band

explanation.surface: A wife grabs a big ring and shouts with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud shout of excitement.

clue.text: Reminder to be punctual

definitions.meaning: a cue given to an actor who forgets a line

explanation.surface: A nudge to arrive on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is a cue to someone, and as an adjective it means on time.

clue.text: Speaker and I love sacred music

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: A speaker declares a love of church music.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large choral work on a religious theme.

clue.text: English money I need to change in Holland

parts.note: L is the pound sterling sign, English currency

indicators.note: to change means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone needs to exchange pounds while in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Leiden is a university city in the Dutch province of South Holland.

clue.text: Favour people with time for promotion

parts.note: to prefer is to favour
men means people

explanation.surface: Someone backs staff with long service for advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferment is advancement to a higher position or office.

clue.text: Radio buffs make poor players

explanation.surface: Radio fans make bad actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hams are amateur radio operators and also bad actors who overdo it.
